mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over three consecutive quarters signals weakening consumer demand, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations deteriorate.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 declines for three quarters but S&P 500 produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of those instances, or if the correlation between GDPC1 and SPX returns weakens to r < 0.2 over any 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 6-month increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average signals expansion in manufacturing output, which historically drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If INDPRO rises for six months but S&P 500 produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of those instances, or if the correlation between INDPRO and SPX returns weakens to r < 0.15 over any 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5.5% signals monetary tightening, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as discount rates rise and corporate borrowing costs increase.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises above 5.5% for three months but S&P 500 produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of those instances, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS and SPX returns weakens to r < 0.2 over any 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.5% signals labor market weakness, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations deteriorate.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises above 5.5% for three months but S&P 500 produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of those instances, or if the correlation between UNRATE and SPX returns weakens to r < 0.15 over any 5-year rolling window.
